question: What is GraphReFly's first-principles identity?
decision: reactive universal reduction layer; not LLM-limited; performance first-class
rationale: any high fan-in/fan-out → information reduction → push is a legitimate segment; LLM is the current primary focus, not the boundary

question: pre-1.0: lock the wedge or not?
decision: do not lock the wedge, horizontal narrow-waist
rationale: reverses R11 (memory+harness wedge); every primitive must serve ≥2 segments (F-NO-WEDGE-CUT)

question: User mental anchor?
decision: graph-first; describe() first-class output
rationale: the graph is the shared cognitive anchor for humans + LLMs, faster to understand than line-by-line code

question: L4 verb set?
decision: 8 verb closed set: node/graph/batch/state + producer/derived/effect/mount
rationale: operator is not a verb (it is node sugar)

question: Node vs Graph responsibilities?
decision: Node is thinnest (no inspection cruft); Graph piles on convenience+inspection, the sole entry point
rationale: a bare node works but has no inspection; g.* sugar auto-registers the inspection index

question: What is an operator?
decision: operator = node sugar (need not go through derived); not recorded in the spec; describe shows the real name
rationale: each language implements independently, never enters parity

question: handle shape?
decision: handle = pure data (pool_id, handle_id), no methods
rationale: serializable/snapshotable/wire-transferable; node≠handle (node has up/down methods)

question: fn-body send/receive message API?
decision: ctx.up(msgs)/ctx.down(msgs); one msgs array = one Wave; may mix tiers
rationale: abolishes actions.emit/forward/backward; the substrate boundary unifies on up/down

question: tier set?
decision: 9 tier: DIRTY/DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE/COMPLETE/ERROR/TEARDOWN + PAUSE/RESUME (control tier-0)
rationale: closed set; PAUSE/RESUME are orthogonal to the value flow

question: PAUSE/RESUME shape?
decision: [[PAUSE, lock_id]]; lockset; caller generates the id; same id is idempotent; RESUME of an unknown id is no-op
rationale: so multiple pause sources do not fight each other

question: message representation?
decision: in-process tuple / wire protobuf decoupled; conversion happens at the wire-bridge boundary
rationale: tuple is debug-friendly; protobuf is compact; the two layers are not forced to agree

question: batch shape?
decision: declarative (success → commit / throw → rollback) + bctx.rollback escape; commit is always implicit
rationale: eliminates the forgot-to-commit class of bugs; the 3 languages naturally align

question: cross-runtime?
decision: each runtime has a local dispatcher + wire bridge; DIRTY across the wire has the same priority as DATA; the user wires the mesh themselves
rationale: R12 DIRTY consistency; the mesh is not GraphReFly's concern

question: formalization depth?
decision: γ: markdown spec + TLA+ + cross-impl property tests
rationale: for our own discipline (prevent drift), not for multi-implementation (c aspirational)

question: When does equals trigger?
decision: equals substitution only when there is exactly 1 DATA within the wave; 0 is irrelevant; ≥2 does not intervene
rationale: with multiple DATA there is no longer any skip-fn benefit -- SUPERSEDED by D49 (Opt-3: no auto-equals-substitution; see R-resolved-undirty)

question: SENTINEL?
decision: a protocol concept (absence-of-DATA is decidable); the concrete sentinel value is per-language (TS undefined / Rust None / Py sentinel)
rationale: same semantics, representation decoupled

question: resubscribe after terminal?
decision: terminal-is-forever by default; resubscribable is opt-in
rationale: the default semantics are clean and the TLA+ state space is small

question: messageTier config?
decision: messageTier = compile-time const table; custom message type extension is cut
rationale: 9 tier closed (D9); adding a tier = changing the spec

question: are onMessage/onSubscribe replaceable?
decision: substrate-fixed, not replaceable; observation uses the inspector (read-only — does not modify/emit node state, but observe via subscribe still activates a cold node, see R-observe); to insert logic add a node
rationale: F-NO-IMPL-DEFINED; cut the user-customized protocol stack

question: pool required for 1.0?
decision: LocalSync + LocalAsync; the dispatcher keeps a pluggable pool trait
rationale: WorkerPool/RemotePool etc. added once the wire bridge matures

question: ownership of dispatcher/pool?
decision: dispatcher first-class; pool hangs off the dispatcher; graph binds a dispatcher (default process-global)
rationale: multi-tenant/sandbox isolation is natural

question: unit of concurrency?
decision: graph = causal domain = concurrency domain = single-threaded; compute parallelism via pool callback; true parallelism via multi-graph + wire bridge; Rust drops the actor model; Py drops the subgraph lock; rewire intra-graph only
rationale: the wave protocol is lock-free; graph boundary = concurrency boundary is explainable; subgraph reverts to pure organization

question: store?
decision: ctx.state is per-node private (implicit is OK); graph-level shared memory = an explicit node+dep
rationale: private state does not violate graph-first; shared memory must be inspectable

question: parity mechanism?
decision: behavioral conformance replaces structural Impl; cross-track-ledger retired
rationale: parity downgrades from symbol-set alignment to protocol-behavior conformance; operator/sugar/inspection are per-language and never enter parity

question: snapshot/restore?
decision: topology + cache + factory-name; restore re-resolves by name; incremental changeset; inline fn marked local-only
rationale: fn cannot be serialized, hence the factory registry pattern

question: central config singleton?
decision: fully dissolved: messageTier=const; onMessage/onSubscribe=substrate-fixed; operational config=graph/dispatcher opts; clock=graph-local monotonic; the only global singleton=default dispatcher; the freeze mechanism disappears
rationale: L3.C graph=causal domain is naturally isolated; config drift + freeze timing complexity is eliminated

question: how is sugar registered?
decision: the sugar→ctx-fn conversion is strictly at the graph layer; dispatcher/node only accept (ctx)=>void
rationale: each language's sugar is free, dispatcher/node are unified → this feeds behavioral parity (D24)

question: cleanup hook?
decision: ctx.onDeactivation + ctx.onInvalidate (2 hooks); cut onRerun (0 callsites) / onResubscribableReset (1 → ctx.state)
rationale: internal state reset belongs to the ctx.state lifecycle, cleanup only handles external resources + INVALIDATE

question: ctx.state lifecycle?
decision: default fresh-lifecycle wipe; ctx.state.persist(boolean?) retains
rationale: latches like frozen-context auto-clear; persist crosses the lifecycle

question: error + cancellation?
decision: throw → ERROR (graph-layer catch); cancellation defaults to no-cancel, {switch:true} opt-in + AbortSignal via ctx
rationale: JS/Py throw is the norm; cancellation as an async pool feature is least-surprise

question: typed error?
decision: error=unknown (Node<T> single generic)
rationale: typed error causes a type-combinatorial explosion; cross-language Box<dyn Error>/Exception is the top type

question: package structure?
decision: each language a self-contained complete package (@graphrefly/ts·rust·py) + a coarse-grained wire bridge; no cross-language peer-deps
rationale: sheds D080/D206 + the 9.5× machine tax; abandons the never-functional TS-on-Rust-substrate fantasy

question: wire codec?
decision: wire=protobuf schema-codegen (a single .proto doubling as wire+protocol contract IDL); implementation deferred post-1.0
rationale: DR-2 IDL single source

question: §5.11 ctx-level exposes tier?
decision: §5.11 amend: ctx-level (node/producer) is a protocol-facing power surface that deliberately exposes tier; value-level (derived/effect/operator) is the §5.11-compliant primary
rationale: ctx.down's one-wave-multi-tier atomicity (terminal-with-final-value) is something the emit/error methods cannot express

question: add IDL to parity?
decision: A+C: behavioral conformance + the L6-Q3 .proto doubling as protocol contract IDL; codegen the interface skeleton (lightweight structural single source)
rationale: pure behavioral loses the structural guarantee; the .proto has to be written anyway, so buying interface-shape consistency at zero extra cost

question: async-result-at-paused-node?
decision: goes into the pause buffer + RESUME replay
rationale: consistent with PAUSE buffering DATA; lock_id scope = node-level pause_lockset

question: graph responsibility overload?
decision: do not introduce a separate domain concept yet (narrow-waist first); record the escape hatch
rationale: if the inspection boundary vs concurrency boundary conflict actually materializes, introduce a domain (one domain contains multiple graphs)

question: conformance hard scenarios?
decision: must include: cross-graph diamond / async-result-at-paused-node / INVALIDATE×ctx.state×onInvalidate / mixed sync-async diamond / PAUSE lockset multi-source; spec amendment list (§5.10/5.11/6.1/7.1 + 3 new)
rationale: otherwise behavioral parity is an empty promise

question: dispatcher opts structure?
decision: grouped {limits, observability, policy}
rationale: avoids the cognitive load of a flat dozen-plus keys

question: CSP-0: canonical messageTier const table (numbering + START placement)?
decision: 7-tier const table: 0 START(handshake) / 1 PAUSE·RESUME(control) / 2 DIRTY(notification) / 3 DATA·RESOLVED(value) / 4 INVALIDATE(settle) / 5 COMPLETE·ERROR(terminal) / 6 TEARDOWN; immediate <3, batch-deferred ≥3
rationale: old-spec numbering with PAUSE/RESUME↔DIRTY swap (control before notification); START=10th handshake type, D9's 9 protocol types occupy tiers 1-6; amends R-tier numbering

question: CSP-0: dynamicNode/track(dep) disposition vs D4 8-verb + D22 rewire?
decision: carry as intra-graph node construction variant (NOT a verb): superset deps declared at construction + track(dep) read-selection per invocation; unread-dep update fires fn then equals-absorbs; same first-run gate; inter-graph N/A (cross-graph deps only via wire bridge)
rationale: distinct mechanism from rewire (per-invocation read-selection vs dep-set mutation); D22 bounds all tracked deps to one causal domain

question: CSP-0: meta companion stores substrate or presentation?
decision: presentation/graph-layer, NOT substrate: static annotations (description/type/range/...) → describe metadata via g.node opts; reactive annotations → explicit nodes (D23); substrate node carries zero meta machinery; meta.owner ABAC is presentation/multi-agent
rationale: D5 node=thinnest with zero inspection cruft; meta is pure annotation feeding describe (graph owns inspection)

question: B10: synchronous feedback-cycle / re-entrant fn semantics — queue (A), reject (B), or require-async (C)?
decision: reject, not iterate (B, owned at graph level): a node fn that during its invocation transitively re-drives one of its own deps so the same node's fn would re-enter before its wave completes is a wave-level protocol ERROR. Detection is node-local and free — refuse to enter the fn-run while the node's own in-wave flag (_insideRunWave) is already set, and throw; the graph layer catches the throw → [[ERROR,e]] down (D30), located at the cycle-closing node, wave aborted. The core neither queues (A) nor bounds-then-runs the cycle. Legit accumulation = per-node ctx.state (scan), not a topological cycle. Async feedback crossing a turn boundary (async pool) is out of scope. No maxFnRerunDepth — precise flag detection supersedes the blunt depth cap
rationale: A normalizes imperative-control-flow-as-topology (feedback_no_imperative) and does not root-fix; B fixes the root with zero new structure by checking the already-existing _insideRunWave flag; dispatcher stays a pure invoke funnel (F-DISPATCH-ALL); error ownership is graph-level per the wave-level error category (D30); surfaced by CSP-1 /qa (backlog B10)

question: B11: what does a depless source do with an upstream-forwarded control message (INVALIDATE/DIRTY/TEARDOWN) at the terminus?
decision: the source self-ACTS only on a message with a coherent round-trip: INVALIDATE → HONOR the invalidate-request (clear cache→SENTINEL, fire onInvalidate, broadcast INVALIDATE downstream = self _invalidate; the down-cascade clears the reachable downstream cone; a node guard may deny it per R-observe, dropping silently). DIRTY → DROP/no-op (a source has no downstream-driven recompute; self-dirty would wedge downstream awaiting a settle that never comes). TEARDOWN → DROP/no-op (source lifecycle is source/graph-owned, not destroyable by a downstream request; revisit on a real cascade-teardown-up consumer). Dep-bearing intermediates only forward upstream control (no self-action); the source is the single actor, the down-cascade the effect
rationale: R-ctx-up/DR-5 deliberately lists INVALIDATE as up-allowed (unlike PAUSE/RESUME which have lockset handling) — the only self-consistent reason to allow it up is for the terminus source to honor it (DS-1 L1.11 'invalidate-request'); it is a cache-drop request not an imperative WRITE (the next value still comes from the source side), so it respects no-imperative + source-owns-value; DIRTY/TEARDOWN have no coherent terminus action. Closes the F-NO-IMPL-DEFINED gap (B11)

question: pre-CSP-2 gate 3: pin the inspection data shapes (describe schema / observe stream protocol / profile metrics)?
decision: describe = flat JSON-serializable snapshot {name?; nodes:DNode[]; edges:{from,to}[]; subgraphs?}, DNode={id (stable mount-aware :: path, auto-numbered when unnamed), name?, factory (real operator name per D6/L1.5), status (R-status-enum), value? (absent=SENTINEL/never-emitted), deps:id[], meta? (static annotations, R-meta-presentation)}; edges derived (R-edges-derived); explain mode = causal-chain subset; renderers are pure fns over the snapshot. observe = read-only enveloped EGRESS (NOT a graph node — avoids self-observation island, D19 read-only), item ObserveEvent={path, msg, tier, seq (graph-local clock, D26)}; one shape for single/subtree/whole-graph. profile = opt-in accumulated-counter snapshot {waves; nodes:Record<path,{invokes,emits,resolved,errored,duration?}>}, backed by an opt-in dispatcher/graph recorder (F-DISPATCH-ALL invoke funnel), NEVER on the thin node (R-node-thin), default-off (F-PERF). All three share the mount-aware :: path key + status/tier/seq metadata. Streaming describe / live-topology = an observe topology-event, DEFERRED to CSP-2 viz
rationale: upholds R-node-thin (profile→dispatcher recorder, not node); observe read-only egress avoids self-observation island + honors D19; consistent with the already-drafted R-describe/R-observe (only pins exact fields + adds R-profile). Inspection is per-language, never in parity (D24) — these rules DOCUMENT the cross-lang contract (covers_by:[], no conformance/TLA+), they do not gate parity

question: clean-slate @graphrefly/ts: how to roll out the operator/upper-layer libraries from pure-ts (~49 operators + 5 upper-layer subsystems)?
decision: Catalog-first: before the CSP-8 dogfood, using the frozen pure-ts (D41) as the authoritative reference, systematically re-derive the complete operator library + upper-layer subsystems (sources/composition/storage/data-structures/render) onto the new substrate, NOT pulled by dogfood. The re-derivation must align with the clean-slate new semantics (R-rom-ram RAM accumulator per B13, SENTINEL=prevData===undefined, push-on-subscribe, two-phase), re-thinking each edge case rather than copying 1:1; each operator gets a describe snapshot test (D39). operator/sources/composition/storage/data-structures are per-language (D6/D24) and never enter parity; the sole exception is rewire=substrate, which goes through conformance (C-8). Accepting the con: time to D1 value is slower, accepted. Scheduling CSP-2.5 (substrate rewire) → CSP-2.6 (sources + operator-opts base) → CSP-2.7 (operator catalog) → CSP-2.8 (upper-layer subsystems), CSP-8 consumes the complete library
rationale: the user prioritizes 'zero upper-layer discard + completeness' over time-to-value; general operators naturally serve ≥2 segments (satisfying F-NO-WEDGE-CUT, not an R11-style vertical wedge); freezing pure-ts as a reference avoids knowledge loss; rewire is the known gap in project_rewire_gap, which Catalog-first fills naturally

question: how to handle the old packages @graphrefly/graphrefly (facade, D32 already retired D080/D206) + @graphrefly/pure-ts v0.49?
decision: freeze as read-only reference: no further development, used as the authoritative reference for 'what exists, what semantics, what edge cases' when re-deriving operators/upper-layers (D40) onto clean-slate; delete once @graphrefly/ts reaches intent-parity. The CLI/parity-tests/demos dependencies on the old packages must be migrated or retired together before deletion
rationale: no-backward-compat permits deletion, but the knowledge value is highest during the re-derivation period, so deleting too early = forcing git archaeology; D32 already decided the facade architecture is retired

question: CSP-2.5: rewire (setDeps/addDep/removeDep) substrate semantics — mid-wave behavior, first-run gate, cache, rejects, API shape?
decision: Ratify the TLA+-verified (126k states, 0 violations) + 34-integration-test-validated port-model rewire design (docs/research/rewire-design-notes.md Q1–Q7) for the clean-slate substrate, adapted to the floor: (Q2) PRESERVE the first-run gate _hasCalledFnOnce — rewire is partial, never re-arms (R-first-run-gate); added deps enter prevData=SENTINEL and the fn guards via prevData===undefined. (Q7) PRESERVE cache for activated compute nodes (R-rom-ram). (Q1) added dep with cached DATA pushes [DIRTY,DATA] (R-push-subscribe); SENTINEL dep → START only. (Q3/Q6) removeDep clears the dep's dirty contribution; if it was the sole dirty contributor and the node was dirty, auto-settle. Surgical/Option-C: kept deps untouched (subscription + DepRecord survive), only removed deps unsubscribe+discard, added deps fresh-subscribe; DepRecord-ref dispatch allows free reorder. Mid-wave rewire (between dep deliveries) ALLOWED; mid-fn rewire (_insideRunWave) REJECTED — now floor-mandated by D37/R-reentrancy (a fn re-driving its own topology mid-wave is the feedback-cycle ERROR), not merely a follow-up; reentrant rewire (another in flight) REJECTED. Rejects: self-dep, cycle (DFS O(V+E)), terminal this (completed/errored), adding a non-resubscribable-terminal dep (wedge); resubscribable-terminal deps allowed. removeDep to zero deps ALLOWED (degenerate fn-no-deps, cache preserved, no auto-deactivate; SD-3). No version bump (topology≠DATA). INTRA-graph only (D22); cross-graph via wire bridge; graph-layer mount-aware g.rewire wrapper is CSP-2.x. SD-1: required fn on all three APIs (fn-deps pairing lock — user fns read data[i]/prevData[i] positionally). SD-2: R-rewire flips active only AFTER cross-axis formal coverage (rewire×{INVALIDATE/terminal/equals/multi-sink}) is modeled, not just the per-node MC + integration tests (F-PROTO-SPEC).
rationale: rewire was fully designed+TLA+-verified+34-test-validated in port-model; clean-slate wave-state concepts map 1:1 so this ratifies proven work rather than re-inventing (D40 Catalog-first: don't discard upper-layer design knowledge). The floor REINFORCES it — D37 upgrades mid-fn-reject to mandatory; R-push-subscribe/R-first-run-gate/R-rom-ram/D22 confirm the Q-resolutions. Substrate prerequisite for higher-order operators (CSP-2.7).

question: CSP-2.6: surface shape for the re-derived catalog (sources + operators) + the operator-opts factory base, given describeKind is dead under D6/D39?
decision: Operators (INCLUDING the 6 landed map/filter/scan/take/distinctUntilChanged/merge) become free-standing operator-factory definitions built on the `node` primitive (NOT the `derived` verb). A single generic graph funnel g.initNode(operator, deps, config?, opts?) instantiates ANY operator factory with the graph's wiring: dispatcher injection + the D30 throw->ERROR boundary + _add real-factory-name registration. This replaces the per-operator Graph methods (the 6 landed g.map/... methods are removed, no-backward-compat). Because instantiation flows through the graph, the factory name is recorded in the graph-layer _entries exactly as today -> describe/observe/profile/find stay UNCHANGED (_entries-based) and the node stays thin (R-node-thin intact, no new node field on the canonical path; NodeOptions.factory? reserved only for standalone graph-less operators). The pure-ts operatorOpts/partialOperatorOpts/gatedOperatorOpts trio is NOT ported: operatorOpts's sole job (describeKind:'derived') is dead under D6/D39/R-describe (factory = real operator name); only the partial / terminalAsRealInput flags survive, carried per-operator via the funnel's flags. Async sources (timer/interval/fromPromise/fromAsyncIter + fromAny/NodeInput<T>) are binding-layer producer-based sugar (D40, feedback_async_sources_binding_layer): timer/interval = pool:'sync'+pausable:false; fromPromise/fromAsyncIter = pool:'async'; cleanup via ctx.onDeactivation (D28); emit only via ctx.down, with setTimeout/Promise confined to source bodies (R-no-raw-async). No substrate change and NO spec amendment (per-language D6/D24, never parity; only rewire is substrate/conformance). SD: resolve the latent substrate edge first -- _shouldBufferOnPause buffers async-pool late emits even when pausable===false, contradicting R-pause-modes' false carve-out; ship async sources on the sync-pool default OR fix _shouldBufferOnPause via /spec-amend+conformance before any pool:'async'+pausable:false source ships (backlog).
rationale: Free-standing operator defs are tree-shakeable + extensible (user priority: catalog completeness over 49 hardcoded Graph methods). The generic g.initNode funnel keeps the Graph as the single wiring + inspection point (D5) with MINIMAL change -- no DAG-walk discovery, no node->graph back-ref, node stays thin (R-node-thin), and describe/observe/profile are untouched. D27 preserved (the operator body is still a (ctx)=>void wrapped at the graph layer); D6 preserved (real factory names recorded at initNode->_add). The operatorOpts trio doesn't port because describeKind was its only purpose and that concept is dead in clean-slate. Sources are binding-layer per feedback_async_sources_binding_layer; substrate verified feasible (depless producer + captured ctx.down late-emit) without a spec change.

question: PAUSE buffering precedence: how does `pausable` mode (R-pause-modes) interact with async-result buffering (R-async-paused) for `pausable:false` and for an async LEAF SOURCE in `true` mode? (B20 + its twin, surfaced by the D43 sources.)
decision: `pausable` mode is the OUTER gate over R-async-paused buffering. (1) false: ignore PAUSE/RESUME ENTIRELY — never gate recompute, never buffer, regardless of pool (sync/async) or node kind (leaf/compute); the node keeps producing through any PAUSE. This DOMINATES R-async-paused (resolves B20). (2) true (default): PAUSE is backpressure on recomputation/propagation only — an async COMPUTE node's (deps>0) in-flight recomputation result buffers when paused (R-async-paused/C-2), but a LEAF SOURCE's (depless) own external down() — sync OR async (timer tick / promise resolve / state.set) — is NOT gated, delivered immediately. (3) 'resumeAll': production-gating mode — buffer the node's own tier-3/4 settle slice incl. a leaf source's own (sync/async) production, replay on final-lock RESUME. Discriminator leaf-vs-compute = deps.length===0. Impl in _shouldBufferOnPause: false->return false; resumeAll->buffer; true->buffer only `!_insideRunWave && asyncPool && deps>0`. Formal: wave_async_paused.tla parameterized by Mode+IsLeaf, invariant NoBufferWhenIgnoring, TLC-green across true/false/leaf/resumeAll + mutation-verified.
rationale: Resolves a genuine under-specification between two ACTIVE rules — R-pause-modes (false=ignore; true leaf-source carve-out) vs R-async-paused (async result at paused node buffers) — which gave OPPOSITE answers for pausable:false+async (B20) and true+async-leaf-source with no stated precedence. The chosen precedence follows R-pause-modes' OWN rationale ('PAUSE is backpressure on recomputation/propagation; production-gating is resumeAll's job') — production is gated only by resumeAll, never by true/false. Surfaced by D43 (CSP-2.6 async sources: timer/interval pausable:false + fromPromise/fromAsyncIter async leaf sources). Extends D10 (pause modes) + DR-3 (async buffering); does not supersede them. C-2 baseline (async compute node) is preserved.

question: CSP-2.7 — how do operators form topology, given D43 already locked the funnel/factory shape?
decision: Operators form graph topology ONLY via [declared deps (static, construction-time)] or [rewire (D42, dynamic)]. Calling node.subscribe() on another graph node from inside an operator fn body to form ongoing topology is BANNED — it creates an edge describe cannot show (an island), violating D3/R-edges-derived/D39. A depless source bridging EXTERNAL async (no graph-node deps) is exempt (already D43). Multi-source combinators (merge/zip/concat/race/combine/combineLatest/withLatestFrom) = static deps + partial + ctx.state (queue/phase/winner/tuple-equals). Dead-inner handling is carried by the substrate via DepRecord.terminal + terminalAsRealInput; the pure-ts subscribeOr/trySubscribeOrDead helpers are NOT ported. The operatorOpts/partialOperatorOpts/gatedOperatorOpts trio is NOT ported (describeKind is dead, D43). DROP pausable (no-op identity — clean-slate nodes handle PAUSE/RESUME natively) and interval-as-operator (it is a source, lives in sources.ts).
rationale: D3 graph-first requires describe to be truthful; internal subscribe = an unexplainable island. The landed merge factory already proves the dep-based shape works. Reusing the substrate wave machinery avoids a second subscription stack. Per-language (D6/D24), never in parity.

question: CSP-2.7 — what shape do time-based operators take under R-no-raw-async?
decision: Split reactive-core from time-sugar. Notifier-driven forms (sample/buffer/window gated on a reactive notifier node) = pure dep-based, shipped in the first cut. Wall-clock-arithmetic forms (delay/debounce/debounceTime/throttle/throttleTime/audit/auditTime/timeout/bufferTime/windowTime) MUST NOT use a raw setTimeout in the operator body (R-no-raw-async / check-no-raw-async.ts); they are ABSENT from the first cut and deferred to backlog (B23), triggered by a resettable/cancellable time-source primitive (async still confined to sources.ts) or a mature async pool. The first-cut docs must state the absence explicitly (no silent cap).
rationale: Notifier-forms are more reactive-pure and immediately shippable; forcing wall-clock forms onto a fixed timer source yields semantically imprecise operators (violates D40 per-operator edge-case re-derivation). delay/timeout need multi-concurrent/resettable timers that are intrinsically a source-layer concern. Per-language (D6/D24).

question: CSP-2.7 higher-order operators (switchMap/exhaustMap/concatMap/mergeMap/flatMap): what substrate mechanism wires the runtime-created inner nodes, given D45 bans internal subscribe and D37 + the async-pool probe block every in-fn / async path to self-rewire?
decision: Add a SUBSTRATE self-triggered, wave-boundary-deferred dep-set mutation affordance (ctx.rewireNext) supporting BOTH addDep and removeDep (option beta). A node fn may, during its run, REQUEST a mutation of its OWN dep set; the request is queued and APPLIED by the dispatcher at the committed wave boundary (after the current wave settles, and after a batch() commits or the final-lock RESUME), as a fresh wave, reusing R-rewire surgical/Option-C semantics (D42). Drain is deterministic: per-node FIFO in issue order, nodes in causal order. A no-net-change request is a no-op; an oscillating net-changing request every boundary is a user-level runaway (like an infinite producer), not a substrate-detected error. This is NOT the D37 mid-fn reject — IMMEDIATE in-fn self-rewire still throws (R-reentrancy); the deferral moves application to a turn boundary where _insideRunWave is false. Inners become VISIBLE self-deps (D45/D3; a describe snapshot shows currently-live inners). removeDep is REQUIRED (beta over read-gate-only alpha): read-gating masks OUTPUT but cannot stop an abandoned inner's still-running source — only removeDep -> _deactivate -> onDeactivation tears down upstream work (switchMap abortInFlight: cancel the in-flight LLM/fetch) and bounds memory (drop completed inners). Architecture: ONE substrate dep-set with {read-mask(track) + add + remove + wave-boundary-deferred self-mutation}; dynamicNode (D35, construction superset + track-by-index) and a future autoTrackNode (runtime append-only discovery + track-by-ref) are read-mask sugars that NEVER remove; the *Map family are sugars that add+remove; sugar names stay distinct (D5/D6). *Map inner-lifecycle folding: inner COMPLETE -> rewireNext(remove) (no downstream COMPLETE unless source done AND no live inner; completeWhenDepsComplete:false + terminalAsRealInput); inner ERROR -> forward, mergeMap does NOT cancel siblings; inner INVALIDATE -> absorbed at the operator; source ERROR -> remove all inners; abortInFlight = the removeDep->onDeactivation teardown. PREREQUISITES (gating): R-rewire-deferred draft + formal wave_rewire_deferred.tla (rewire x wave-boundary axis) TLC-green + conformance C-11 green per arm BEFORE flip-active (F-PROTO-SPEC + SD-2); B15 (fn-swap handle GC) MUST land first. *Map EXCLUDED from the CSP-2.7 first cut until these clear.
rationale: Read-gate (append-only, the dynamicNode/autoTrackNode model) is correct for OUTPUT but cannot stop upstream WORK (a subscribed source keeps running; only unsubscribe->_deactivate->onDeactivation cancels) — so switchMap cancel-the-superseded + abortInFlight + memory bounding require REMOVE, hence beta. Deferring to the wave boundary clears D37 by construction (turn boundary, not synchronous re-entry) and keeps inners visible (D45/D3). Unifying at the substrate (one dep-set, many sugars) avoids three overlapping primitives (D5/D6). Probe: the async pool does NOT defer the fn (dispatcher/index.ts:48 + node.ts:692, _insideRunWave set during any fn run), so the wave boundary is the only legal application point.

question: Do operators ship tiered across packages (L4-Q7: core in main, time+higher-order in @graphrefly/<lang>-operators) or all in the main package?
decision: All operators ship in the main @graphrefly/ts package as free-standing tree-shakable factory definitions (graph/operators.ts), exported from the single index; there is NO @graphrefly/<lang>-operators subpackage. The main package is sideEffects:false + ESM (tsup), so an unused operator is dropped at the consumer's bundle step — pay only for what you import, without a package split. SUPERSEDES the L4-Q7 tiered-subpackage lock (and the @graphrefly/<lang>-operators mention in L6-Q2): its bundle-size rationale is obviated by ESM tree-shaking, and clean-slate has no heavy operator deps (time operators deferred to B23; async confined to sources). Per-language (D6/D24); higher-order *Map (pending D47 substrate) also lands in main.
rationale: D43 already made operators free-standing tree-shakable factories citing tree-shakability, and the 6 landed operators + sources sit in the main package (sideEffects:false). A separate package adds build/version/peer-dep complexity for zero bundle-size benefit under ESM tree-shaking. Retiring L4-Q7's split keeps the decision log consistent with the code (single source of truth).

question: Auto-substitute DATA->RESOLVED on value-equality (D15), or keep every occurrence as DATA and push dedup to the operator layer?
decision: REMOVE substrate auto-equals-substitution (Opt-3, supersedes D15). (1) Every value-occurrence is ALWAYS emitted as DATA; a node never substitutes DATA->RESOLVED on value-equality, and the substrate no longer inspects the per-wave DATA count for substitution. fromIter([1,1,1]) -> [DATA,DATA,DATA]. (2) RESOLVED is RETAINED, narrowed to ONE meaning: a node DIRTY'd in phase 1 that produced NO tier-3 value this wave emits exactly one RESOLVED to clear the downstream dirty (filter-reject, zero-dep un-dirty, INVALIDATE arriving at a never-populated cache, batch-rollback DIRTY-balance). It never means 'value unchanged'. This undirty RESOLVED is SUBSTRATE-SYNTHESIZED (a value-level operator just returns without emitting; the substrate emits the balancing RESOLVED) so operator bodies stay clean (R-primary-api-clean); an operator MAY emit its own DATA/RESOLVED explicitly as an escape hatch if a corner case needs it. Tier-3 wave exclusivity holds (>=1 DATA XOR 1 RESOLVED), re-justified as occurrence-vs-undirty. (3) Dedup ('skip an expensive recompute / suppress an unchanged emission') is OPT-IN at the operator layer (distinctUntilChanged with its own eq via ctx.state, or an operator fn early-return); NodeOptions.equals (substrate) is REMOVED. Glitch-free diamond (R-two-phase + R-diamond) is orthogonal and PRESERVED.
rationale: equals-absorption overloaded RESOLVED (occurrence-with-unchanged-value vs dirty-clear) and destroyed 'an occurrence happened' info, breaking event-counting/accumulating operators (probe: fromIter([1,1,1]) -> [DATA,RESOLVED,RESOLVED]; take(3) -> [1] not [1,1,1]). Narrowing RESOLVED to undirty-only keeps occurrences as DATA (take/scan/skip/elementAt/reduce/snapshot correct without special-casing), turns RESOLVED into a clean undirty signal, and drops a per-emit equals check on the common path. Accepted cost (F-PERF): auto-suppression of unchanged-value cascades is gone; dedup is now opt-in via distinctUntilChanged (explicit control).

question: INVALIDATE × PAUSE precedence: what does a dep's INVALIDATE do to a paused (default-mode) compute node's coalesced recompute? (cross-axis gap surfaced by the CSP-5 Rust control/terminal slice /qa, finding A — the INVALIDATE-side analogue of D44's async×PAUSE precedence)
decision: (Q1) a dep INVALIDATE while N is paused PROPAGATES downstream IMMEDIATELY (consistent with immediate DIRTY; not gated/buffered in default mode — buffer-replay is resumeAll's job; the downstream un-wedges its DIRTY via the INVALIDATE's dirty-clear, no wedge). (Q2) it SUPERSEDES that dep's buffered paused dep-wave: clear the dep to SENTINEL + drop its pending change, then RE-DERIVE pendingRecompute (paused_dep_wave_occurred) from whether ANY dep still carries a buffered change (ATTRIBUTED cancellation). N recomputes on final-lock RESUME ONLY if some dep still has a live buffered change; if the INVALIDATE leaves no buffered change the paused recompute is CANCELLED (N already settled to SENTINEL via its own INVALIDATE — nothing to recompute). A later DATA on the same dep RE-ARMS the buffer: [DATA(v1),INVALIDATE,DATA(v2)] → N recomputes with v2 on RESUME. Scoped to default ('true') mode; resumeAll buffers+replays tier-3/4 on its own path.
rationale: the current impl leaves paused_dep_wave_occurred set after an INVALIDATE clears the sole buffered dep → on RESUME N recomputes against a now-SENTINEL dep: a redundant undirty RESOLVED for a SENTINEL-guarding fn, and a spurious TERMINAL ERROR for a non-guarding fn (its .unwrap() panics → [[ERROR,e]] via D30). Attributed cancellation kills the spurious recompute without dropping a surviving dep's legitimate update (multi-dep). Parity-consistent latent gap in BOTH arms (TS yields a garbage value instead of ERROR). Extends D10/D44 (pause modes); references R-invalidate-idempotent. Formal wave_paused_invalidate.tla TLC-green (327 states) + ChangedImpliesLive mutation-verified load-bearing.

question: Does describe() render construction-time deps or current/live deps after a rewire (C-8 immediate / C-11 *Map deferred), and how are runtime-created inner deps (bare graph-less nodes) shown?
decision: describe() is a LIVE point-in-time snapshot: edges derive from each registered node's CURRENT deps (live _deps, re-read at call time), NOT the construction-time snapshot — so every edge corresponds to a REAL current subscription (D3 / R-edges-derived truthfulness) and rewire (C-8 + C-11) is reflected. A live dep absent from the graph inspection index (a runtime-created *Map inner / bare fromAny node) is AUTO-DISCOVERED on each describe() call as a snapshot node — synthesized stable id; status/value from the node getters; factory taken from the inner's OWN NodeOptions.factory (the field D43 RESERVED for 'standalone graph-less operators', set by the free initNode at the inner's creation), else '?' when absent. Chosen variant = B2 (live auto-discovery + the D43-reserved factory): inners are NEVER persistently registered in _entries — best-effort live capture, no register/unregister churn on fast inner turnover (switchMap creates/destroys an inner per source value). The persistent-registry variant B1 (graph-in-body / ctx.graph / a node→graph backref) is REJECTED: it pierces D27 (node/dispatcher see only (ctx)=>void) + R-node-thin and churns the index. First cut auto-discovers ONE level (the direct inner deps); transitive discovery (an inner carrying its own subtree) is a follow-up. Live-topology STREAMING (rewire deltas) stays an observe topology-event, deferred to viz (R-describe / B4) — a point-in-time read is NOT streaming. Adds an optional Node.deps readonly getter (R-node-iface) + realizes NodeOptions.factory? (D43-reserved, OFF the canonical wave path, R-node-thin intact).
rationale: R-edges-derived self-contradicts once rewire exists: 'construction-time deps' vs 'every edge has a real protocol subscription' — after removeDep (C-8) a construction edge is decorative (no subscription), violating D3; for *Map (C-11) construction deps OMIT the live inners. A live-dep snapshot restores truthfulness and realizes D47/C-11 ('a describe snapshot shows currently-live inners'). B2 gives NAMED inners WITHOUT graph-in-body or a persistent registry — matching the user's best-effort-capture intent (point-in-time, no churn) by reusing D43's already-reserved factory field. Per-language inspection (D24, never in parity, no conformance). Amends R-edges-derived ('construction-time'->'current/live') + R-describe (snapshot reflects live deps + auto-discovery + NodeOptions.factory naming). Surfaced as backlog B34(a) by the CSP-2.7 /qa; locked via /design-review (B2 over A over B1).

question: CSP-2.7 wall-clock time operators (delay/debounce(Time)/throttle(Time)/audit(Time)/timeout/bufferTime/windowTime) were deferred by D46/B23 pending 'a resettable/cancellable time-source primitive or a mature async pool'. Given the higher-order *Map machinery (D47/ctx.rewireNext) landed 2026-05-30 AFTER D46/D47 were locked (2026-05-29), do these still need a new primitive?
decision: No new primitive. Wall-clock time operators are authored as COMPOSITIONS over the already-active substrate. debounce/throttle/delay/audit/timeout = *Map(switchMap/exhaustMap/mergeMap/concatMap) over the EXISTING timer(ms) source: the timer's onDeactivation clearTimeout IS the reset/cancel — switchMap's removeDep->onDeactivation cancels an in-flight timer, the declarative equivalent of pure-ts's imperative clearTimeout-then-setTimeout debounce (frozen ref time.ts, D41). bufferTime/windowTime = buffer/window(notifier) over the EXISTING interval(ms) source (notifier-driven forms already first-cut per D46). setTimeout/setInterval stay confined to the timer/interval source bodies (R-no-raw-async clean, check-no-raw-async passes); operator bodies carry ZERO raw async. REFINES D46's deferral RATIONALE ONLY (D46's notifier-driven first-cut shape UNCHANGED): the 'needs a resettable time-source primitive OR a mature async pool' premise is obsoleted by the D47 *Map landing — the *Map+timer swap is the third path D46 could not rely on (D46/D47 locked 2026-05-29; *Map landed 2026-05-30). Time operators REJOIN the CSP-2.7 implementable catalog: per-language (D6/D24), NO /spec-amend, NO substrate change, NO conformance (operators never in parity). REJECTED (B) a dedicated resettable-timer source — its reset channel would need a new tier (D9 constitutional) or an imperative reset (R-no-imperative); (C) allowlisting a time/ operator dir for raw setTimeout — D46 forbids raw setTimeout in operator bodies + spreads async beyond sources. Per-operator edge: trailing-value-flush-on-source-COMPLETE defaults to DROP (clean-slate changes-only, consistent with merge B13); opt-in flushOnComplete for RxJS parity. VERIFIED before lock: a throwaway switchMap+timer debounceTime probe is GREEN incl. the discriminating boundary-deferred removeDep->onDeactivation->clearTimeout cancel timing (v1 then v2 within the window emits only v2; the cancelled timer-1 never fires) — load-bearing premise empirical, not assumed.
rationale: Reuses the landed + conformance-green *Map(C-11)+timer+buffer(notifier) machinery — zero substrate change (F-PERF/F-NO-WEDGE-CUT), no new primitive to maintain. It is the declarative reactive equivalent of pure-ts's own clearTimeout/setTimeout debounce, so the semantics have precedent. Alternatives B and C both fight the floor (new tier / imperative reset / async-outside-sources). The B23/D46 blocking premise was a stale-by-one-day artifact (the *Map mechanism that dissolves it landed the day after D46 locked) — a verify-premise-before-greenfield catch; probe-verified before lock per the three-gate edge-case-design discipline.

question: B28 -- under D49 (no equals-absorption) a dynamicNode re-emits DATA when an UNREAD (untracked) dep changes, losing the auto-quiet-on-unread-deps property. Restore it via a substrate read-mask (track records the per-invocation read-set; a wave whose DIRTY contributors are all outside the last read-set is absorbed), or keep auto-quiet as an opt-in composition?
decision: Keep fn-controlled / opt-in (Option B, enriched per user). NO substrate read-mask. A dynamicNode's fn (a ctx-fn with EXPLICIT ctx.down -- node.ts dynamicNode = NodeFn) ALREADY fully controls whether an unread-dep change propagates: it inspects which deps delivered this wave (ctx.depRecords[i].batch non-empty) and DECIDES. To stay QUIET on an unread-dep-only wave it early-returns WITHOUT ctx.down -> the substrate synthesizes ONE undirty RESOLVED (D49/R-resolved-undirty, RESOLVED's single meaning = UNDIRTY) -> downstream sees DIRTY->RESOLVED = no new value, quiet. To PROPAGATE it calls ctx.down([[DATA,..]]). VERIFIED (throwaway probe GREEN): prime A,B; unread B-change -> fn early-return -> DIRTY,RESOLVED downstream (NO redundant DATA); read A-change -> DIRTY,DATA. ctx.track(i) stays a pure value-reader (depRecords[i].latest = this-wave value if delivered else cache). Downstream distinctUntilChanged remains an ALTERNATIVE for value-based dedup. CLOSES B28. REJECTED (A) the substrate read-mask: although VERIFIED sound (read-set = f(read-values, ctx.state), both stable on an unread-only wave -> output provably unchanged), it HARD-CODES ONE policy ('a wave driven only by unread deps is always absorbed') -- but whether an unread-dep change SHOULD re-trigger the node is USE-CASE-DEPENDENT (some compositions want B to re-fire D, some do not; both legitimate). An automatic substrate mask REMOVES that choice; leaving it to the fn PRESERVES both at zero substrate cost and keeps dynamicNode from being the lone exception to D49's opt-in-dedup-everywhere. RE-OPENABLE only if a real consumer needs the mask AND per-invocation read-set recording proves cheap. ZERO behavior change (fn-controlled quiet already works on the landed substrate); NO /spec-amend formal/conformance; R-dynamic-node statement updated.
rationale: The suppress-vs-propagate decision on an unread-dep change is a POLICY that varies by use case (user's framing) -- so it belongs to the dynamicNode fn, not an automatic substrate read-mask that hard-codes 'always suppress'. D49 already narrowed RESOLVED to exactly UNDIRTY, which is the clean quiet signal: fn early-return -> substrate undirty RESOLVED -> downstream un-dirtied without a redundant DATA. This gives per-composition control + value-based distinctUntilChanged as a complement, at zero substrate cost (F-PERF), and keeps dynamicNode from being the lone exception to D49's opt-in-dedup-everywhere. The sound-but-heavier read-mask (A) is documented + re-openable. Probe-verified before locking the refinement (verify-premise discipline). Per-language: track + undirty RESOLVED are substrate, but no arm needs an impl change -- current behavior already IS this.

question: CSP-2.8 data-structures (reactive-list/map/index/log) -- what shape is the mutation INPUT surface, given the floor's no-imperative-triggers + the user's allergy, and that the frozen pure-ts reference exposes 4-6 imperative mutation methods (.append/.set/.delete/.upsert/...) per structure? (Fork A, the gating decision for CSP-2.8.)
decision: A3 (hybrid dual boundary). The reactive structure's CORE is a reactive RAM accumulator over a command/value stream (R-rom-ram; the exact scan-vs-state-snapshot core + snapshot-vs-delta primary emission = the shared-core / Fork-B follow-up, NOT this decision). The mutation INPUT surface is DUAL-FORM: (1) imperative methods (.append(v)/.set(k,v)/.delete(k)/.upsert(..)/.clear()/...) as the EXTERNAL input boundary -- legitimate `state`-verb sugar (D4: state.set IS the sanctioned way external non-reactive values enter a graph; a data-structure mutation is a state transition, not a forbidden reactive-recompute trigger); AND (2) the SAME surface WIDENED to accept a reactive source -- a method/constructor takes `T | Node<T>` (and/or construct-from-command-source) so an in-graph reactive producer drives the structure with ZERO imperative glue (feedback_no_imperative_wrap_as_primitive: widen the helper's args to T|Node<T> so callers opt into reactive control without forcing the abstraction). REJECTED A2 (pure-reactive scan over a command stream, no methods): the EXTERNAL input boundary is UNAVOIDABLY imperative -- a non-reactive event (UI click / network callback) must enter the graph through some imperative call; A2's 'zero imperative' is ILLUSORY at that boundary (it only relocates `.append(v)` to 'emit a command', forcing external callers to construct command messages, with in-graph composition the sole real gain). REJECTED A1 (imperative-only): forces imperative glue for in-graph composition. A3 keeps the CORE purely reactive (scan/state -- describe-able, no island, D3/R-edges-derived) while serving BOTH the external boundary (ergonomic imperative methods, state-verb-legitimate) and in-graph composition (Node-accepting widening). The imperative methods are NOT the 'remove when no caller depends' case -- the external boundary always has a caller (the structure exists to receive external input). Per-language (D6/D24, never in parity, no conformance). Old-core dissolutions carried into impl (NOT forks): equals:a===b REMOVED (D49 -- idempotent no-op judged by the structure's own version counter, not substrate equals); describeKind dropped (D6/D39/D43 -- real factory names); reactive-log empty/never-set lastValue = SENTINEL (D49 narrowed RESOLVED to undirty -- replaces the old [[RESOLVED]]-for-empty dual-role; prevData===undefined detection); reactive-index byPrimary = a derived node over the ordered snapshot.
rationale: The external input boundary cannot be made non-imperative (the non-reactive world must enter somewhere) -- so the floor's no-imperative-TRIGGERS rule (which targets faking reactive recomputation via emit/callback) is NOT violated by a state-input boundary (D4 sanctions state.set). The user's own durable pattern (no_imperative_wrap_as_primitive) prescribes exactly the T|Node<T> widening for a primitive that inevitably re-exposes an imperative helper. A3 yields a reactive, inspectable core + ergonomic external boundary + glue-free in-graph composition; A2 trades external ergonomics for an illusory purity; A1 forces glue. No probe needed (API-shape design; substrate facts scan=R-rom-ram accumulator, state verb, D49 commands-as-DATA already established). GATING decision for CSP-2.8 data-structures; the shared reactiveCollection core, scan-vs-state, and snapshot-vs-delta (Fork B) build on this boundary shape.

question: CSP-2.8 composition (stratify / stratifyBranch / topologyDiff) re-derivation onto the clean-slate substrate (describe = flat live snapshot D39/D51; topology only via declared deps or rewire D45/D42)?
decision: (1) topologyDiff = pure static analysis over two describe snapshots -> DescribeChangeset; ZERO old-core deps; MECHANICAL port, adapted to the D39 DescribeSnapshot shape (nodes/edges/subgraphs). (2) stratifyBranch = re-derived as a DECLARED-DEP 2-dep node (deps=[source, rules], classifier fn), NOT the frozen reference's direct cross-graph node.subscribe() -- which forms an edge describe cannot show (a D45/D3/R-edges-derived ISLAND VIOLATION in the frozen ref). The two-dep gating is the normal two-phase wave (both deps settle); the rules.cache peek is replaced by reading the dep value (R-push-subscribe delivers it on subscribe); describeKind dropped (D6/D39, real factory name). (3) stratify = a branch-builder composition over stratifyBranch; FIRST CUT = STATIC rules (N fixed branches declared at construction, each a stratifyBranch declared-dep node -- inspectable, zero rewire). DYNAMIC rules (a rules-node change adds/removes branches at runtime via ctx.rewireNext/D47) DEFERRED to a follow-up (backlog), matching the operator first-cut discipline (static before dynamic) + no-silent-cap disclosure. The cross-graph source case = wire bridge (D22/D33), not an in-process node proxy. Per-language (D6/D24, never parity, no conformance).
rationale: topologyDiff is already clean (pure data over snapshots). stratifyBranch's frozen direct cross-graph subscribe is a latent D45 island violation; declared-deps fix it for free AND make the branch inspectable. Static-rules-first keeps the first cut declarative + rewire-free; dynamic rules reuse the just-landed rewireNext (D47) when a real consumer needs runtime branch reconfiguration.

question: CSP-2.8 storage (tiers / WAL / content-addressed / cascading-cache) -- substrate/spec or binding-layer, and how does its pervasive async I/O interact with the sync wave core (F-SYNC-CORE)?
decision: Storage is BINDING-LAYER (per-language D6/D24, never in parity -- same disposition as async sources D43), NOT substrate/spec. The async I/O (IndexedDB/fs/sqlite/SHA-256/WAL) is confined to the storage adapter, NEVER entering the sync wave core (F-SYNC-CORE). Integration: (1) PERSISTENCE = an OBSERVE-SINK (D39 observe = read-only enveloped egress) the adapter subscribes to, plus an async writer that persists snapshots/diffs at the wave-close boundary. flush = FIRE-AND-FORGET by default (low reactive latency; durability errors absorbed, mirroring the frozen cascading-cache fireAndForget) + opt-in SYNC-FLUSH for durability-critical consumers (blocks the next commit until the write settles). (2) HYDRATION/restore = a BOOTSTRAP-PHASE pooled async op (D20 pool) that batch()-replays persisted frames into the graph through the normal input boundary (D12 batch), NOT a wave-core operation; a ready() signal gates on hydration. (3) ROLLBACK on wave-throw = best-effort async discard in the adapter, not a sync-core guarantee. (4) cascading-cache = a GRAPH-LAYER REACTIVE read-through cache (each entry a state node, R-rom-ram) fronting the async tiers as a miss-source (fromPromise-style async source, D43) -- distinct from the persistence adapter. Tier interfaces (StorageBackend/SnapshotTier/AppendLogTier/WAL/content-addressed) are binding-layer APIs, async-aware per runtime. Versioning (cid/schema/caps, B3) stays deferred.
rationale: Storage is async I/O; F-SYNC-CORE confines async to pools/sources/wire-bridge, and D43 already set the precedent that async, per-language concerns are binding-layer (never parity). Storage attaches as an OBSERVER (reads egress + writes async), never participating in the sync cascade -- so the observe-sink + bootstrap-pool model fits cleanly. Fire-and-forget default keeps reactive latency low (most apps); durability-critical opts into sync-flush. cascading-cache is genuinely reactive (state nodes) so it lives at the graph layer, the async tier as a fromPromise miss-source.
